business_domains.description: This domain encompasses all user account-related business capabilities, including user registration, authentication (sign-on and sign-off), account profile management, and user preferences. It manages the complete lifecycle of user identity in the system — from creating new accounts to updating personal information (name, email, address, contact details), managing login credentials, and storing user preferences such as language settings and favorite product categories. It also covers profile-based personalization features such as banner display options. The domain owns all data and logic pertaining to who the user is, how they authenticate, and what their preferences are.

This domain covers the product catalog and inventory management capabilities of the pet store. It manages the hierarchical structure of the store's offerings: categories (e.g., types of pets), products (e.g., specific breeds), and items (e.g., individual purchasable units with pricing, supplier, and attributes). It also handles inventory tracking — checking stock availability for specific items — and product search functionality that allows customers to find products by keyword. The domain is responsible for browsing experiences, from the main catalog view down to individual item details, and it manages the relationship between items and their suppliers.

This domain manages the transient, session-based shopping cart experience. It handles the core business capabilities of adding items to a cart, removing items from a cart, updating item quantities, and calculating the cart's subtotal. It acts as a temporary holding area for selected items before the customer proceeds to checkout. The domain maintains the in-progress shopping state across user interactions within a session, tracking each selected item's quantity, price, and stock availability. It bridges catalog browsing and order placement by collecting selected items prior to order confirmation.

This domain manages the full lifecycle of customer orders — from the moment a customer confirms a purchase through checkout, to order persistence, order status tracking, and retrieval of order history. It handles the conversion of a shopping cart into a formal order, capturing shipping and billing address details, payment information (credit card type, card number, expiry), order date, and total price. It manages the individual line items within each order, tracks order status, and handles inventory updates upon order placement. It also supports generating unique order identifiers via sequences and provides customers access to their historical orders.
